summary: Renders geometry with a constant material color or color map, independent of scene lighting, while still exposing common MAT render-state, deform, and texture sampling controls.

key_params.name: applyprojmaps
key_params.note: Apply projection maps from camera/light workflows

key_params.name: applypointcolor
key_params.note: Multiply or apply geometry point color

key_params.name: colormap
key_params.note: Texture map used as material color

key_params.name: colormapcoord
key_params.note: SOP texture coordinate attribute or coordinate source

key_concepts: Constant MAT renders a material with constant color or texture color independent of scene lighting, making it useful for UI, masks, debug geometry, and projection-map looks.
Projection maps can be applied without having the projection color altered by the normal lighting model.
Point color and alpha can multiply the material result, so geometry attributes still matter even when the shader is light-independent.
Color maps use the same texture-sampling contract as other MATs, including SOP UV layers, POP texture coordinate attributes, screen-space coordinates, and triplanar mapping.
Common MAT pages still control deform, blending, depth test, alpha test, culling, wireframe, polygon offset, and color-parameter interpretation.
common_gotchas: Constant MAT ignores scene lighting, which is useful for UI/projection/debug materials but wrong for lit physical surfaces.
Color maps need valid texture coordinates unless using screen-space or triplanar mapping.
Common MAT blending, depth test, cull face, and alpha test still affect render output even though the shading model is simple.
If geometry uses capture/deform attributes, the Deform page must be configured just like other MATs.
